discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the opening of neutrino astronomy beyond the MeV scale with IceCube
motivation: Kamiokande's detection of neutrinos from SN1987A opened neutrino astronomy at MeV energies. Francis Halzen conceived and led IceCube, a cubic-kilometre detector built into the Antarctic ice, which took this field to energies a million times higher. In 2013 IceCube reported the first convincing evidence for a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV to PeV energies. Later it found a neutrino coincident with the flaring blazar TXS 0506+056 (2017–18), observed steady emission from the active galaxy NGC 1068 (2022), and imaged the Milky Way in neutrinos (2023). These results give a new, unabsorbed view of the most energetic processes in the universe and help address the old problem of where cosmic rays come from. The achievement rests on decades of patient, careful development of the detector and analysis. It reflects the long-term commitment to large underground and under-ice facilities that leads to basic discovery.
